newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prepares for Zaire talks on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prepares for Zaire talks on Wednesday.

text.p: South Africa is preparing to host the first face-to-face talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire and rebel leader Laurent Kabila in Cape Town on Wednesday, government sources said on Friday.
"We have pencilled in Wednesday, but President Mobutu has not agreed to any details yet," said one source. Kabila had earlier said he would talk only about a transfer of power.
On Thursday, South African President Nelson Mandela formally invited Mobutu and Kabila, whose forces have overrun about half of Zaire, to talks in South Africa.
Mobutu's security adviser and chief negotiator, Honore Ngbanda, said in Kinshasa on Friday that Mobutu had accepted the invitation, but gave no further details.
Kabila said in a telephone interview from Lubumbashi, Zaire's mining capital and current headquarters of his rebel alliance, that he would talk only about a transfer of power.
"There will be no protracted negotiations with Mobutu, never, never," he said. "Maybe we have been misunderstood. The issue is about transfer of power, otherwise we march on Kinshasa."

U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said on Thursday that Mandela's invitation, issued after Ngbanda and Kabila visited Cape Town on Wednesday, was to discuss transitional arrangements leading to elections in the country ruled by Mobutu for 32 years.
South African officials said Mandela was expected to leave Cape Town for his country home on Sunday for two or three days of rest.
Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who has choreographed South Africa's initiative for peace in Zaire, was scheduled to leave on Saturday for talks in the United States with Vice President Al Gore.
A spokesman said Mbeki would discuss bilateral relations and the situation in central Africa's unstable Great Lakes region, including Zaire.
He said Mbeki was scheduled to return around midday on Wednesday and could be available for talks that day.
South African government sources stressed the arrangements for Wednesday were tentative and could be brought forward or delayed.

One source said a meeting on Tuesday was possible. Another said Mobutu's aides had raised a question about whether he was well enough after treatment for prostate cancer to travel to South Africa and suggested he might prefer a meeting in neighbouring Congo.
All the sources said Cape Town was the most likely venue if the talks take place.
